description: Aterin developed the Lunar Landing Site Navigator — an interactive 3D web platform for evaluating candidate landing sites at the Moon's South Pole. Powered by live NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data and LRO LOLA topography, our tool visualizes real-time solar illumination, vacuum terrain horizons, Earth optical libration, and Direct-to-Earth communication windows to help mission planners and educators compare mission scenarios in seconds.
summary: Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive 3D web application that translates complex lunar ephemeris and LRO LOLA topographic data into intuitive, real-time visualizations for the Moon's South Pole. Designed for mission planners, educators, and the public, our platform solves a critical CLPS and Artemis challenge: rapidly evaluating how small shifts in landing coordinates or launch schedule delays impact solar power generation, shadow survival, and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows. Featuring a scroll-driven 3D space onboarding experience, a 360° vacuum horizon sky-dome, an interactive global Moon globe, first-person astronaut surface views, vertical vs. horizontal solar array modeling, and live NASA JPL Horizons API verification, it enables side-by-side mission scenario trade-off analysis in seconds.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO & HOW DOES IT WORK?

Lunar Landing Site Navigator bridges the gap between complex planetary ephemeris systems (such as NASA JPL Horizons and LOLA datasets) and agile mission planning. At the Moon's South Pole, the tiny 1.54° axial tilt creates "Peaks of Eternal Light" right next to -230°C Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs). A 500-meter shift in landing location or a two-week launch delay can turn an 89% sunlit mission into a 12% shadow failure.

Our web application combines a 60 FPS analytical orbital mechanics engine with live server-side queries to the official NASA JPL Horizons API (/api/horizons) to provide instant visual feedback across five core modules:

1. Interactive 3D Scrollytelling Onboarding: A scroll-driven 3D journey from Earth orbit to the Lunar South Pole that visually explains the 1.54° axial tilt, zero-atmosphere vacuum horizons, Earth's optical libration (±7.9° lon / ±6.7° lat), relay satellites, and 500m landing dispersion zones.

2. Synchronized Multi-View 3D & 2D Workspace:

- Global 3D Moon Globe Mode: Displays the real-time lunar terminator, 3D Sun and Earth directional vectors, curated landing sites (Shackleton Ridge, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton, Haworth Crater, Statio Shiv Shakti, Apollo 11, Apollo 17), and click-to-place custom coordinates.

- Local 3D LOLA Topographic Orbital View: Renders steep polar crater geometry and real-time shadow casting.

- 360° Interactive Astronaut Surface View: First-person 360° look-around camera on the lunar surface showing the surrounding crater horizon, cardinal compass markers, textured Earth, and blazing Sun.

- 360° Horizon Sky-Dome & 2D Regional Map: Plots the 360° terrain elevation mask (H_terrain), geometric vacuum horizon, 29.5-day solar path, and Earth libration wobble loop.

3. Solar Array Geometry & Thermal Survival Calculator: Compares Vertical Polar Tracking Solar Masts (cos(elevation)) against Horizontal Deck Panels (sin(elevation)), computing real-time Solar Flux (W/m²), countdown timers to Sunset/Earthset, and required battery capacity (kWh) to survive the longest continuous shadow period at a 250W heater load.

4. Side-by-Side Scenario Comparison & Optimal Window Finder: Compares Scenario A vs. Scenario B with one-click schedule slip buttons (+7 Day Delay, +14 Day Delay, 500m into Crater, Shift to Higher Ridge), an automated "Optimal Window" scanner across the 708-hour lunar cycle, and JSON telemetry export.

5. Live NASA JPL Horizons DE441 Telemetry Verification: Queries NASA's JPL Horizons System (coord@301) for Target 10 (Sun) and Target 399 (Earth) to verify azimuth, elevation, and Earth-Moon Perigee/Apogee range in km.

INTENDED IMPACT & BENEFITS

- For Mission Planners (CLPS & Artemis): Accelerates trade-off coordination between science and engineering teams when hardware delays or launch slips require rapid site or date re-evaluation.

- For Educators & the Public: Toggles seamlessly between "Planner Mode" (raw telemetry, libration angles, flux metrics) and "Educator Mode" (plain-language insights contrasting equatorial Apollo missions with South Pole physics).

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Frontend & Backend: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS

- 3D & Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, HTML5 Canvas & SVG

- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub, Vercel

- AI Disclosure: Code architecture, mathematical implementation, and team patch icon were developed with the assistance of AI tools (Claude and Gemini).
